contexts.text: There is in each and all things with man a resemblance of a marriage...
There is an idea or resemblance of the soul and the body in each thing with man...
Unless these two make one by a kind of a resemblance of a marriage...

For in all the good which proceeds from the Lord there is a resemblance of Himself; and thence a resemblance of Heaven: whereas in the good which is from man there is a resemblance of the man; and, as man from himself is nothing but evil, there is a resemblance of Hell.
According to the likeness of this it is done here...
And any likeness = a resemblance of those things which are from the Divine.

Resemblances of the things which are from the Divine are made by men when with the mouth they speak Divine things, and also actually do such things as are commanded by the Divine... when yet at heart they think quite differently... In the other life, evil Spirits make resemblances of the things which are from the Divine...
Goods and truths... make in man a resemblance of Heaven.
It is explained by its resemblance or image.

The whole man is a resemblance of his own will and his own understanding thence; consequently, a resemblance of his own good and derivative truth; or a resemblance of his own evil and derivative falsity...
As everything of the body is produced from the soul, thus to the resemblance of it...
Thereby cause that in the world also there is a resemblance of Heaven.
[Swedenborg footnote 1.]. That between good and truth there is a resemblance of a marriage. References.
For the body is an effigy of the mind, because it is formed after its resemblance.
There is a certain resemblance of conjugial love with some...
That the good of love is like fire... References.
To which they give a resemblance of reason.
Every love which proceeds from the form of love itself is a resemblance thereof.
Charity... forms (faith) to a resemblance of itself; and therein presents an image of itself.
Everything in which there is force, wills to produce a resemblance of itself; and to multiply its own species...
That the Divine, which is Life itself, would make the Human a resemblance of itself, thus also Divine.
For the Spiritual inflows into the Natural, and disposes it to correspondence, thus to a resemblance of itself.
